Working notes — request routing

Options seen: A standard queue, B priority desk, C regional office; D is invalid and must not be chosen.

Evidence:
- C succeeded only for claim requests from the south region: REQ-2400 (small), REQ-2407 (large), REQ-2408 (small).
- C was rejected for non-claim requests tested: refunds from south (REQ-2401, REQ-2403) and east (REQ-2405, REQ-2409), invoices from east (REQ-2402, REQ-2406). Shipment case (REQ-2404) rejected option D.
- Therefore, C is not generally valid for refunds, invoices, or shipments.

Working rule:
- If request type = claim AND region = south, route to C.
- Otherwise, do not use C; avoid D entirely.
- A vs B for other cases remains untested. No successful A/B choice has been observed yet, so do not infer priority from size or urgency.

Signals that did NOT affect outcome:
- Small vs large amount.
- Requester name/desk.
- Subject-line phrases such as “same as last month,” “regional office,” “client asking twice,” “scanned, not typed,” “second attempt,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt.”
- East vs south region by itself, except C validity appears tied to south + claim.

Next useful tests:
- Non-claim south requests to see whether A or B should be used.
- Claim requests in east/other regions to see whether C is region-specific.
- Any A/B success/failure to establish routing for non-special cases.

Working notes — request routing

Options: A standard queue; B priority desk; C regional office; D invalid, never choose.

C:
- Valid only observed for claim + south: REQ-2400, 2407, 2408.
- Rejected for refunds/invoices/shipments tested; not general.

A:
- Accepted: invoice + north small (REQ-2416); shipment + east small (REQ-2413); refund + east small (REQ-2418).
- Rejected: refund + south small (REQ-2410); refund + north small/large (REQ-2411, 2415, 2419); claim + north small (REQ-2412); claim + east large (REQ-2414); shipment + south large (REQ-2417).
- So A is type/region-specific, not general. No large A successes observed. B remains untested.

Working rules:
- Claim + south: C, but memo says claim procedure changes soon; re-test before relying.
- Otherwise avoid C and D.
- A may be used for observed matches: refund+east, invoice+north, shipment+east. For other non-claim combos, A has failed or is untested; try B where possible.
- Do not infer from amount, requester, desk, or subject phrases. Region and request type matter.

Signals not affecting outcome:
- small vs large; names/desks; phrases (“second attempt,” “scanned,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt,” etc.).
- East/south alone is not enough; combine with request type.

Next useful tests:
- B on A-rejected non-claim cases: refund north/south, shipment south.
- Claims in east/north/other regions with C/B.
- Large invoice+north, large refund+east, large shipment+east to see if size changes A.
- Any B success/failure to establish B routing.

Working notes — request routing

Options: A standard queue; B priority desk; C regional office; D invalid, never choose.

Observed:
- C: valid only claim+south (REQ-2400, 2407, 2408). Rejected refund/invoice/shipment. Not general.
- A: accepted invoice+north small (REQ-2416, 2426); shipment+east small (REQ-2413, 2422); refund+east small (REQ-2418). Rejected refund south/north, claim north/east, shipment south. No large A success.
- B: all new tests rejected: refund+north (2420); shipment+south small/large (2421, 2428, 2429); invoice+south large (2423); claim+north large (2424); shipment+north large (2425, 2427). No B success yet. Avoid B unless new evidence.

Rules:
- Claim+south: C. Memo says claim procedure changes soon; re-test.
- Memo says shipment procedure changes soon; re-test shipment before relying on A for shipment+east.
- Otherwise avoid C and D.
- Use A only for observed matches: refund+east, invoice+north, shipment+east, all small unless retested.
- Do not infer from amount, requester, desk, or subject phrases. Region and type matter.

Signals not affecting outcome:
- small/large, names/desks, phrases (“no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “asking twice,” “anything missing,” “same as last month,” etc.).
- East/south alone insufficient; combine with type.

Next useful tests:
- A on large invoice+north, large refund+east, large shipment+east to test size.
- C/B for claims outside south.
- Post-change shipment tests.
- Any B success.

Working notes — request routing

Options: A standard queue; B priority desk; C regional office; D invalid, never choose.

Observed:
- C: accepted claim+south small (REQ-2400, 2407, 2408). Rejected claim+south large (2433), claim+north large (2436), refund/invoice/shipment. So C = small claim+south only; re-test after claim procedure change.
- A: accepted refund+east small (2418, 2438); invoice+north small (2416, 2426); shipment+east small (2413, 2422). Rejected refund south/north, claim north/east, shipment north small (2431), shipment east/north large (2435, 2439), invoice+south large (2434). No large A success.
- B: all rejected, including new refund+north/south (2420, 2432, 2437), shipment+south/north, invoice+south, claim+north/east. No B success. Avoid B unless new evidence.

Rules:
- Claim+south small: C. Claim+south large: not C; unknown.
- A only for observed small matches: refund+east, invoice+north, shipment+east. Do not use A for shipment+north, any large A, or other region/type pairs.
- Avoid C except small claim+south; avoid D.
- Memo: shipment procedure changes soon; re-test shipment before relying on A for shipment+east. Claim procedure changes soon; re-test claim+south small.
- Do not infer from requester, desk, or subject phrases. Region, type, and now size matter; small/large can affect routing.
- Signals not affecting outcome: names/desks, phrases (“no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “asking twice,” “anything missing,” “same as last month,” etc.). East/south alone insufficient; combine with type and size.

Next useful tests:
- A on large refund+east, large invoice+north; confirm large A always rejected.
- C/B for small claims outside south.
- Post-change shipment and claim tests.
- Any B success.

Working notes — request routing

Options: A standard queue; B priority desk; C regional office; D invalid.

Current rules:
- Claim: small + south -> C. large + south -> B. C rejected for small claim east/north. B has no other observed claim success. Do not use C outside small claim+south. Other claim region/size unknown.
- Invoice: north -> A (small 2416, 2426; large 2448). large east -> B (2442). A rejected invoice+south large; B rejected invoice+south. So use A for invoice+north; B for large invoice+east.
- Refund: east small -> A (2418, 2438). B rejected refund north/south, including large north and small north. Do not use B for refund. Other refund unknown.
- Shipment: unstable. A accepted east small earlier, but 2443 east small rejected A. A rejected north small, east/north large. B rejected south/north. Re-test before relying on any shipment rule. Avoid A for shipment+north; avoid B for shipment unless new success.

Avoid B except large claim+south and large invoice+east observed. Avoid C except small claim+south. Avoid D.

Size matters: claim+south small/C vs large/B; invoice+north works as A both sizes; large invoice+east/B.

Signals not affecting: requester, desk, phrases (“second attempt,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “asking twice,” “same as last month,” “scanned not typed,” “came through regional office,” etc.). Region, type, and size matter; combine all three.

Next useful tests:
- B for other large claim regions; A/B for small claims outside south.
- Post-change shipment tests; do not trust previous shipment maps.
- Refund outside east small; invoice+east small.
- Confirm repeat of large invoice+north A and large claim+south B.

Working notes — request routing

Options: A standard queue; B priority desk; C regional office; D.

Known valid:
- Claim: small+south -> C. large+south -> B.
- Invoice: north -> A. large+east -> B. large+south -> D.
- Refund: east+small -> A.
- Shipment: unstable; re-test after procedure change. Avoid B shipment generally.

Rejections/limits:
- Claim: A rejected large north, small east, small north. C rejected small east/north. Use C only for small claim+south; B only for large claim+south so far. Other claim region/size unknown.
- Invoice: A works north; B works large east; D works large south. A rejected south small. B rejected south earlier. Use A for invoice+north; B for large invoice+east; D only for large invoice+south.
- Refund: A works east small. B rejected refund north/south, including large north/small north. A rejected north small and south large. Do not use B for refund. Other refund unknown.
- Shipment: A rejected east small later, north small, east/north large. B rejected south/north and now east large. Do not trust old shipment maps.

D is not globally invalid: D accepted large invoice+south. Avoid D otherwise.

Size matters: claim+south small/C vs large/B; invoice+north A both sizes; large invoice+east/B; large invoice+south/D.

Signals not affecting: requester, desk, phrases. Examples: “twice already,” “scanned not typed,” “no rush,” “confirm receipt,” “let me know if missing,” “same as last month,” “before end of day.” Region, type, and size matter; combine all three.

Next tests:
- Claims: B for small outside south; B/C/D for large north/east.
- Invoice: small south/east; D beyond large south.
- Refund: outside east small; C/D options.
- Shipment: post-change tests only.
- Confirm repeats: large invoice north A, large claim south B, large invoice east B, large invoice south D, small claim south C.
